message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
It includes:

| What you’ll need | How to get it |
|------------------|---------------|
| **Project ID** | `gcloud config get-value project` or set it explicitly with `--project=YOUR_PROJECT_ID` |
| **Zone** | Pick a zone that supports GPUs (e.g. `us-central1-a`, `europe-west4-a`). |
| **Service account key** | Create a service account with `roles/compute.admin` and download its JSON key. |
| **gcloud SDK** | Install from <https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install> |

---

## 1.  gcloud CLI command

```bash
# Replace placeholders with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \          # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
  --boot-disk-size="200GB" \
  --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
  --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
  --maintenance-policy="TERMINATE" \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional: custom init script
  --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1" \
  --tags="http-server,https-server" \
  --labels="env=dev,role=compute"
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root disk. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU (`nvidia-tesla-a6000`). |
| `--maintenance-policy` | `TERMINATE` means the VM will be stopped during maintenance. |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restarts if the VM crashes. |
| `--scopes` | Grants full Cloud Platform access. |
| `--tags` | Enables HTTP/HTTPS firewall rules. |
| `--labels` | Optional metadata for cost‑tracking or automation. |

> **Tip:** If you need more GPUs, just change `count=2` (or more) – note that some zones have limits on the number of GPUs per instance.

---

## 2.  REST API (JSON) – `instances.insert`

If you prefer to use the raw REST API (e.g., from a CI/CD pipeline), here’s the exact JSON payload you would POST to:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 200
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "labels": {
    "env": "dev",
    "role": "compute"
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  },
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### How to call it

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

Replace `@instance.json` with the path to the JSON file above, and adjust `my-gcp-project` and `us-central1-a` accordingly.

---

## 3.  Quick sanity check

After creation, verify the GPU is visible:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=us-central1-a --command="nvidia-smi"
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with driver version, memory, etc.

---

## 4.  Optional: Startup Script

If you want to automatically install CUDA, cuDNN, or other libraries, create a `startup.sh` file and reference it with `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh`. Example content:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
apt-get update
apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470
apt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-11-8
```

---

### Recap

* **CLI**: `gcloud compute instances create … --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1"`
* **REST**: POST to `/instances` with `guestAccelerators` field set to the RTX A6000 type.
* **Prerequisites**: Enable Compute Engine API, have a project, choose a GPU‑capable zone.

Happy GPU computing! 🚀
